content:
Let \(s=x+y\) and \(q=x-y\). Since \(x,y\ge \frac12\), we have \(s\ge 1\) and \(|q|\le s-1\).

Using the correct identity
\[
x^3+y^3+x^2y+xy^2=(x+y)(x^2+y^2),
\]
and
\[
x^2+y^2=\frac{s^2+q^2}{2},\qquad xy=\frac{s^2-q^2}{4},
\]
we get
\[
f=\frac{s(2s^2-9s+12)+(2s-3)q^2}{4}.
\]

For \(1\le s\le \frac32\), \(2s-3\le 0\), so
\[
f\ge \frac{s(2s^2-9s+12)+(2s-3)(s-1)^2}{4}
=s^3-4s^2+5s-\frac34.
\]
This is minimized on \([1,\frac32]\) at \(s=\frac32\), giving \(\frac98>1\).

For \(s\ge \frac32\), \(2s-3\ge 0\), so
\[
f\ge \frac{s(2s^2-9s+12)}{4}.
\]
Let
\[
h(s)=\frac{s(2s^2-9s+12)}{4}.
\]
Then
\[
h'(s)=\frac32(s-1)(s-2),
\]
so on \(s\ge \frac32\), \(h\) is minimized at \(s=2\), giving
\[
h(2)=1.
\]
Equality holds when \(s=2\) and \(q=0\), i.e. \(x=y=1\).

Therefore the minimum value is
\[
\boxed{1}.
\]
